learningObjectives.text: What makes the sign come true?

warning.author: Various Chinese storytellers; collected and retold in English by J. Macgowan
warning.locator: THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE; THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE, normalized characters 2737-3601
warning.excerpt: Before very long a great flood will take place in this district, and will sweep everything before it. It will be so sudden that men will not be able to take measures to preserve either their lives or their property--so instantaneous will be the rush of the mighty streams, like ocean floods, from the mountains you can see in the West. My advice to you is to commence at once the construction of boats to carry you and your most precious effects away. When the news first comes that the waters are rising, have them anchored in the creek that flows close by your doors; and when the crisis arrives, delay not a moment, but hurry on board and fly for your lives." rescue.author: Various Chinese storytellers; collected and retold in English by J. Macgowan
rescue.locator: THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE; THE REWARD OF A BENEVOLENT LIFE, normalized characters 9322-9806
rescue.excerpt: Chung replied that at such a time, when a human being was in extreme danger of being drowned, personal interests ought not to be considered at all. He had faithfully obeyed the command of the priest in saving animal life, but how much more valuable was a man than any of the lower orders of creation? "Whatever may happen," he said, "I cannot let this man drown before my eyes," and as the boat just then came alongside the swimmer, he was hauled into it and delivered from his peril.
rescue.note: Quotation from J. Macgowan's English literary collection of folktales; distinguish this written version from a community-wide canon.

narrativeBlocks.title: A warning in a dream
narrativeBlocks.body: A good man is warned in a dream that a great flood is coming — and told to watch the city gate: when the iron statue's eyes bleed, he must flee to the hills.

narrativeBlocks.title: The butcher's cruel joke
narrativeBlocks.body: A butcher hears of the man's daily watch and plays a trick: he smears blood on the statue's eyes. The man sees the 'sign' and runs for the hills.

narrativeBlocks.title: The flood proves the warning
narrativeBlocks.body: And the flood comes — the joke became the prophecy. The warning was real even though the sign itself was faked.

narrativeBlocks.title: The widow and the turtle
narrativeBlocks.body: On the flood waters the man rescues a drowning widow — and a great turtle — and the turtle's later repayment turns the whole tale: kindness is the story's real engine.

narrativeBlocks.title: Macgowan's village tales
narrativeBlocks.body: This story comes through John Macgowan's 1910 collection of Chinese folk tales — a missionary's retelling of village stories, not a canonical scripture.
